BH-2026-0002.title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting in SCORM 2004 debug logs
BH-2026-0002.summary: A user with only repository read permission can append arbitrary values to a persistent SCORM 2004 HTML debug log. Multiple fields are written into HTML and inline JavaScript contexts without contextual encoding. The generated log is stored beneath the web-served client data directory and is anonymously retrievable as same-origin HTML, allowing stored JavaScript execution when another user opens it.

BH-2026-0003.title: Unauthenticated execution of web-exposed Composer vendor maintenance scripts
BH-2026-0003.summary: The web server forwards arbitrary PHP files beneath the Composer dependency tree to PHP-FPM. The deployed tree contains build, test, and maintenance programs intended for command-line execution. Some of these scripts do not reject web-SAPI execution and can perform expensive or state-changing work under the web-service account.

BH-2026-0004.title: Unauthenticated modification of repository File settings
BH-2026-0004.summary: The normal File settings form is protected by `Capabilities::EDIT_SETTINGS`, but the `update` command itself performs no equivalent authorization check. Both a low-privileged user and a fresh unauthenticated session can submit valid settings data and persist changes. The response may later display Permission Denied even though the database update has already committed.

BH-2026-0014.title: Cross-object File download through the Glossary handler
BH-2026-0014.summary: The Glossary download handler authorizes the caller against the selected Glossary but accepts a global repository File object ID and streams that File without checking the File's own repository permission, online state, or relationship to the Glossary.

BH-2026-0020.title: Disclosure of the Composer dependency inventory
BH-2026-0020.summary: The complete Composer dependency inventory is available without authentication. The response identifies exact package names and versions, allowing deterministic correlation with public advisories and significantly reducing the effort required to target dependency-specific attack paths.

BH-2026-0022.title: Unauthenticated SOAP group configuration and stored access-code disclosure
BH-2026-0022.summary: The SOAP `getGroup` method serializes the complete configuration of a caller-selected Group without checking read permission, membership, ownership, or a group-administration capability. The assessed session logic accepted a newly generated, nonexistent session identifier as an authenticated anonymous context, making the object-level authorization failure reachable without a valid account.

BH-2026-0023.title: SOAP clients can enumerate arbitrary users' effective repository permissions
BH-2026-0023.summary: The authenticated SOAP operation accepts an arbitrary subject `user_id` and returns that user's effective operations for a repository object. The server validates only the SOAP session and does not require the caller to be the selected subject or to possess an administrative permission for inspecting other users.
